title: Focusable element hidden from screen readers
user_impact: Keyboard users reach elements that screen readers do not announce — invisible traps.
technical_impact: A tab-reachable element (natively focusable, or tabindex of 0 or more) sits in a subtree marked aria-hidden="true" and is not inert, so keyboard focus lands on it while a screen reader announces nothing; behind an open modal dialog this is only a review hint.

checks.source: WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value and SC 1.3.1; WAI-ARIA 1.2 §6.7 aria-hidden (authors must not hide focusable content); HTML §6.6.3 tabindex, §6.3 inert
checks.applicability: Rendered elements in the sequential tab order (native focusable or tabindex >= 0) that are inside, or carry, aria-hidden="true".
checks.expectation:
Fails (violation, one per element) when an element that the Tab key reaches
is hidden from the accessibility tree by aria-hidden="true" on itself or an
ancestor, also across an open shadow root (aria-hidden applies to the flat
tree): keyboard users land on something that is not announced. Passes when
the element is taken out of the tab order (tabindex="-1"), when the hidden
subtree is inert, when it is not rendered, or when aria-hidden is "false".
Native links and ARIA widgets with tabindex 0 count alike, as does
aria-hidden set by a script after load. Behind an open modal dialog
(aria-modal="true" or an open <dialog>) aria-hidden on the page outside the
modal is the ARIA dialog pattern when focus stays in the dialog; that cannot be
decided statically, so such an element is needs_review, not a violation.
aria-hidden on a control inside the modal itself stays a violation.
